question: What is the primary neurotransmitter released at the neuromuscular junction to initiate muscle contraction?
explanation: Acetylcholine is stored in vesicles at the motor neuron terminal and released into the synaptic cleft to bind post-junctional receptors. [learn more](GNS223_U5_T5#GNS223_U5_T5_h1)

question: How do neuromuscular blocking agents affect a patient's level of consciousness during surgical procedures?

options.A: They block pain pathways while leaving motor function intact
options.B: They induce a deep state of general anesthesia alongside paralysis
options.C: They cause mild sedation followed by progressive sensory loss
options.D: They produce complete paralysis without altering awareness or sensation

explanation: NMBs only affect skeletal muscle tone at the junction and possess zero anesthetic, hypnotic, or analgesic properties, requiring concurrent sedation. [learn more](GNS223_U5_T5#GNS223_U5_T5_h1)

question: Which medication is classified as a depolarizing neuromuscular blocker?
explanation: Succinylcholine mimics acetylcholine to depolarize the motor end-plate, whereas the other options are competitive antagonists. [learn more](GNS223_U5_T5#GNS223_U5_T5_h2)

question: What is the primary mechanism by which nondepolarizing agents prevent muscle contraction?

options.A: They competitively occupy postsynaptic receptors without triggering depolarization
options.B: They permanently destroy stored acetylcholine vesicles in the nerve terminal
options.C: They inhibit the enzyme acetylcholinesterase within the synaptic cleft
options.D: They cause continuous excessive depolarization until muscle stores deplete

explanation: Nondepolarizing blockers sit on the receptor and block access for acetylcholine, stopping the end-plate potential from reaching threshold. [learn more](GNS223_U5_T5#GNS223_U5_T5_h2)

question: A patient with severe acute respiratory distress syndrome is violently fighting the mechanical ventilator despite heavy sedation. Which intervention is most appropriate to improve oxygenation?

options.A: Immediately extubating the patient to allow spontaneous breathing
options.B: Applying physical restraints to all four extremities to limit movement
options.C: Administering a short course of a neuromuscular blocking agent
options.D: Increasing the baseline fractional inspired oxygen concentration to maximum

explanation: Paralytics are used in severe ventilator dyssynchrony to eliminate patient respiratory effort and reduce barotrauma risk. [learn more](GNS223_U5_T5#GNS223_U5_T5_h3)

question: What is a primary clinical reason for administering a neuromuscular blocker prior to endotracheal intubation?

options.A: To stimulate spontaneous coughing and clear lower airway secretions
options.B: To provide profound systemic analgesia and pain relief
options.C: To prevent sudden drops in systemic blood pressure
options.D: To relax the vocal cords and facilitate safe airway insertion

explanation: Relaxing skeletal and laryngeal muscles prevents laryngeal spasm and allows smooth, atraumatic placement of the endotracheal tube. [learn more](GNS223_U5_T5#GNS223_U5_T5_h3)

question: Which rare, life-threatening complication is uniquely associated with the administration of succinylcholine?
explanation: Succinylcholine, alongside volatile anesthetic agents, can trigger malignant hyperthermia in susceptible individuals. [learn more](GNS223_U5_T5#GNS223_U5_T5_h4)

question: Why is succinylcholine strictly contraindicated in patients with extensive third-degree burns or severe crush injuries?

options.A: It induces immediate renal failure by precipitating myoglobin in the tubules
options.B: It provokes a massive efflux of potassium leading to life-threatening cardiac arrest
options.C: It causes an intracellular shift of sodium resulting in severe hyponatremia
options.D: It triggers massive histamine release leading to anaphylactic shock

explanation: Burn and trauma injuries cause extrajunctional receptor proliferation; when succinylcholine opens these channels, potassium pours out into the bloodstream. [learn more](GNS223_U5_T5#GNS223_U5_T5_h4)

question: Which drug acts by chemically encapsulating rocuronium or vecuronium molecules to rapidly reverse neuromuscular blockade?
explanation: Sugammadex is a modified gamma-cyclodextrin designed specifically to bind steroidal blockers and render them inactive. [learn more](GNS223_U5_T5#GNS223_U5_T5_h5)

question: Why must an anticholinergic drug like glycopyrrolate or atropine be given concurrently with neostigmine during reversal?

options.A: To prevent life-threatening tachycardia and systemic hypertension
options.B: To enhance the binding affinity of the paralytic agent to the receptor
options.C: To counteract unwanted parasympathetic side effects such as severe bradycardia
options.D: To accelerate the renal clearance of the encapsulated drug complex

explanation: Neostigmine floods the body with acetylcholine, stimulating muscarinic receptors and causing profound slowing of the heart rate unless blocked by an anticholinergic. [learn more](GNS223_U5_T5#GNS223_U5_T5_h5)

question: What is the name of the monitoring device used to objectively assess the depth of neuromuscular blockade at the bedside?
explanation: The peripheral nerve stimulator delivers electrical current to gauge neuromuscular function using train-of-four responses. [learn more](GNS223_U5_T5#GNS223_U5_T5_h6)

question: Which clinical observation indicates that a patient has sufficiently recovered from neuromuscular blockade prior to extubation?

options.A: The train-of-four monitor shows exactly zero twitches
options.B: The patient opens their eyes spontaneously for two seconds
options.C: The patient is able to sustain a 5-second head lift on command
options.D: The patient responds to painful stimuli by grimacing

explanation: Sustained head lift and strong hand grips prove that adequate muscle strength and upper airway tone have returned. [learn more](GNS223_U5_T5#GNS223_U5_T5_h6)
